source_adaptations: Inserted an offline input-loading adapter immediately after 'import matplotlib.pyplot as plt' (top of the source, before any computation): nk.data() builds URLs under https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neuropsychology/NeuroKit/master/data/ and calls nk.pd.read_csv on them; since the exported 'neurokit2.data' module exposes the pandas instance it uses as nk.pd, the adapter wraps nk.pd.read_csv to redirect that exact URL prefix to the identical bytes staged at /inputs/. This preserves the scientific contract: the same CSV is read through nk.data()'s unchanged code path (verified by smoke test in the setup shell — 30000x3 DataFrame with the expected ECG/PPG/RSP header). No algorithm, parameter, filtering, or plotting change; all imports and scientific calls are unchanged.
unresolved_assumptions: The dataset was retrieved from NeuroKit's 'master' branch (the pinned source lib nk.data() requests); the worker verified it is byte-identical to the file at the notebook's source revision ff419d98, but long-term drift of the master branch cannot be ruled out beyond the pinned sha256 check in stage-inputs.sh (which would fail loudly rather than load altered data).

Column sets and any NaN cells in the four HRV DataFrames (e.g. rarely reported indices) were not manually inspected beyond the produced artifact sizes; single-row structure matched the preparation plan's assumption.

The dependency-asset audit is discovery-based (priority/candidate inspection, whole-catalog review of names and the executed usage), not an exhaustive semantic proof that no installed file contains HRV-like numbers; the four exported tables are the only scientific answer artifacts produced by this analysis.
